name: Chon-Ak-Suu Gorge
near: Grigorievka (Chon-Ak-Suu) on the north shore, at the mouth of the gorge; ≈30–35 km east of Cholpon-Ata, ≈60 km west of Karakol on the Balykchy — Karakol road.
elev: Mouth at Grigorievka ≈1700 m; the lower part of the gorge with camps ≈1900–2100 m (Nomad's Land: 2000 m); alpine meadows and lakes 2200–2500 m, upper pastures up to 3000–3500 m; the peaks Kum-Bel 4200 m and Eshenbulak 4647 m. The exact elevation of the catalog point has not been published.
short: A narrow, forested gorge of the Chon-Ak-Suu river on the slope of Kungey Ala-Too above Grigorievka: Tian Shan spruces up to 50 m tall, a rushing river, and three mountain lakes (Lower, Middle, Upper) farther up the valley. The most visited “wild” spot on the north shore: yurt camps, horses, eagle hunters (berkutchi), and trout grilled over charcoal.
desc: Chon-Ak-Suu (“big white water”) is a gorge 22–35 km long (depending on the source) on the northern slope of Issyk-Kul, parallel to the neighboring Semyonovka (Kyrchyn) gorge; Kok-Bel Pass and dirt roads connect them, so they are often done as a loop. The lower part is a tight rocky canyon with sheer cliffs and spruce forest, which people compare to the Krasnoyarsk Stolby (Pillars); higher up the gorge opens into alpine meadows (2200–2500 m) with three lakes, of which the Upper one at the treeline is considered the most beautiful, and nearby is the bright blue Jasyl-Kol. On the jailoo (summer pasture) there are shepherds' and tourist yurts where they serve trout grilled over charcoal, sell honey, offer horse rides and show eagles. In season (July–August) the lower part is full of cars, vendors and day groups from the pansionats (Soviet-style resort hotels) of Cholpon-Ata; above the lakes there is sometimes an army post that restricts access to the Kazakhstan border. Entry is paid (according to 2025–2026 reviews, with different rates for foreigners); the amount is not officially published.
guide: Don't stop at the first yurts with shashlik and eagles — drive or walk on to where the gorge opens into meadows: that is where the Upper Lake is, with quiet and views of the four-thousanders Kum-Bel and Eshenbulak. Negotiate for the horse in advance and count by the minute: according to reviews, prices are quoted as “from 300–500 som an hour”, and then they charge 20 som per minute. The trout here really is local — it is grilled by the river, but the average bill in a yurt for a group is about 1000 som per person, so ask the price before ordering. If you have a 4×4 and a day, do the loop: up the Grigorievka gorge, over the pass and down the Semyonovka gorge; in a regular car it is better not to go beyond the first kilometers. Spring comes late in the gorge — in May the lakes are still under ice, and in June the meadows bloom.
see: A tight canyon with sheer cliffs and spruce forest; the Chon-Ak-Suu river in a turquoise glacial color; a small waterfall; three lakes (Lower, Middle, Upper) and Jasyl-Kol; alpine meadows with yurts; views of Kum-Bel (4200) and Eshenbulak (4647); eagle hunters and horses at the yurt camps; the loop route over the pass into the Semyonovka gorge.
skip: If you are looking for solitude — in July–August the lower part is jammed with cars, yurts and vendors. If you are in a low-slung car — beyond the first few kilometers the road is “awful”, especially during repairs. If you are already going to the Semyonovka gorge — the landscape is similar; choose one unless you have a day for the loop.
diff: Easy for seeing the lower part (walks from the parking spots, 1–3 h); moderate for the hike to the lakes (ascent to 2500 m, 10–15 km one way) or the loop over the pass; the road higher up needs a 4×4.
when: June — early October. Spring comes late and summer is short; late May — June — the meadows bloom, September — golden autumn and fewer people. Peak crowds — July–August. In winter the road is limited by snow.
hours: The gorge is open around the clock; the barrier/fee at the entrance operates in daytime in season; yurt camps — May–September. There is no Google card (ambiguous result); 2GIS lists no hours.
daytime: Morning (leave Cholpon-Ata by 9:00): fewer cars, and the river water is clearer; by lunchtime there are traffic jams of tour jeeps in the lower part.
how: From the Balykchy — Karakol road, in Grigorievka turn north (signpost); the first kilometers are dirt road/paved in places, then a mountain road. From Cholpon-Ata: marshrutka (minibus) No. 501 or bus No. 401 to Grigorievka ≈200 som (40 min), then a 30 min walk to the entrance of the gorge; taxi 700–800 som (Tonkosti Turizma, 2024–2025). From Bishkek: marshrutka to Grigorievka — 700 som for two (T—Zh, 2022). Jeep tours from Cholpon-Ata 900–1300 som/person (basic) or €32–35/person including Semyonovka and the Holy Lake (2026).
needcar: For the lower part — any car in dry weather (Too.kg); for the lakes and the loop with Semyonovka — a 4×4, or on foot/horseback. Without a car it is realistic: marshrutka to Grigorievka + on foot.
self: Yes: entry is free for pedestrians after paying the fee, and the trail along the river is obvious; for the lakes and over the pass, use navigation and allow extra time; for the upper reaches a guide or a horse is better.
roadtype: Too.kg: a dirt road of decent quality, passable by a regular car; 2GIS reviews 2025–2026: even asphalt in places, narrow sheer sections in others, and broken during repairs; TripAdvisor: “awful roads, better not to go in a regular car”, but people drove a Corolla slowly; beyond the first kilometers — only a jeep (LJ uritsk). Above the lakes there is an army post.
traveltime: Cholpon-Ata → Grigorievka 40 min (marshrutka) / 30 min (taxi); Bishkek → Grigorievka ≈4 h; Karakol → Grigorievka ≈1–1.5 h. In the gorge: to the yurts 15–30 min by car, to the lakes 1–1.5 h by 4×4 or 3–5 h on foot. The jeep loop with Semyonovka takes 8 h.
stay: Yurts in the gorge: ≈2000 som per yurt for 5 people/night, meals ≈400 som (tonkosti.ru); seasonal yurt camps and a campsite by the river (Too.kg). In Grigorievka/Chon-Sary-Oi and Bosteri — guesthouses and pansionats at 2000–3000 som/day (tonkosti.ru); hotels in Cholpon-Ata — see 24.kg 2024.
net: In Grigorievka and at the mouth, all operators have signal; higher up the gorge the signal disappears in the narrow part and appears in places on the meadows. There are no direct measurements; in 2026 Beeline strengthened the neighboring Chon-Sary-Oi/Ananyevo without naming Grigorievka. An offline map is a must.
entry: Barrier of the Issyk-Kul forestry enterprise (Kaktus.media, 10.06.2025): per person — Kyrgyz citizens 20 som, citizens of former USSR countries 100, foreigners 220 som; per vehicle — car 80, large vehicles 170, buses/trucks 300 som. This matches the 2GIS reviews of 2025–2026 (“paid entry, more for foreigners”). The same rates apply in the neighboring Semyonovka (Kichi-Ak-Suu).
transfer: From Cholpon-Ata: marshrutka 200 som, taxi 700–800 som (2024–2025); group jeep tour €35/person or €215 per vehicle (2026); basic excursions 900–1300 som/person (tonkosti.ru). From Bishkek, marshrutka to Grigorievka ≈350 som/person (2022).
bring: A windbreaker/fleece (it is cool in the gorge even in July), shoes for rocks and fords, cash in som (entry, horses, food — no cards), water (higher up, water is scarce), repellent, sun protection, an offline map.
warn: The road above the lower part is narrow, with drop-offs, and broken; do not drive a low car after rain. Horse handlers at the yurts often inflate the price and count “by the minute” — agree on the amount before mounting. Above the lakes there is an army post, and you won't be let through to the Kazakh border. Swimming in the lakes — the water is icy and the shores are boggy. In season there are lots of livestock and dogs near the yurts. The entrance fee is the forestry enterprise's official tariff since 2025 (foreigners 220 som/person + 80 for a car); ask for a receipt.
food: Trout grilled over charcoal by the river in the yurt camps (a guide of ≈1000 som/person for lunch in a yurt on jeep tours, 2026; reviews note inflated prices), mountain honey, kumys and ayran from shepherds, flatbreads, shashlik. The river water is glacial — drink it only after boiling.
reviews: 2GIS: 4.9/5, 350 ratings, ≈100 reviews (07.10.2026). TripAdvisor (Grigorevskoye Canyon): 4.8/5, 36 reviews (07.10.2026). Google Maps: no unambiguous card. Pluses: the scenery, the air, the river, trout, honey. Minuses: roads during repairs, pushy and dishonest horse handlers, inflated yurt prices, crowds in season, the post higher up the valley.
p.sum: There is one way in — from the village of Grigorievka (Chon-Ak-Suu) on the north-shore road, 35 km east of Cholpon-Ata. A regular car can slowly reach the lower part of the gorge (the first ≈10 km to the meadows); to the upper lakes only by jeep or on foot/horseback. The most convenient option is a jeep tour from Cholpon-Ata combining the Grigorievka and Semyonovka gorges (from €35/person in a group, €215–250 per vehicle). On a budget — bus No. 401 or marshrutka No. 501 from Cholpon-Ata (≈200 som) and on foot; there is a forestry barrier at the entrance (foreigners 220 som + 80 for a car), and agree on the horse price before mounting.

p.budget.comfort: ≈6000–15,000 som/person: jeep tour €35 in a group or €250 per vehicle, horse 1–2 h 600–1000, lunch in a yurt
p.permits: No permit is needed as far as the lakes (higher up is the border zone, with an army post). Barrier of the Issyk-Kul forestry enterprise (since 2025): foreigners 220, CIS 100, Kyrgyz citizens 20 som/person; car 80, large vehicles 170, bus 300 som — ask for a receipt.
p.access: With children — by car to the meadows, yes; for older people — by jeep; with a wheelchair — no; with a dog — possible, but there are many shepherd dogs and livestock.
